headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; no direct shared-channel evidence, but B can ingest A-derived outputs via HTTP/API workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is an image-generation system with file-based model inputs and asynchronous queueing; emqx is an HTTP/API-facing broker/scheduler. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, if operators bridge ComfyUI outputs into emqx workflows, attacker-controlled prompt text could be propagated. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into emqx-managed messages or templates
IF emqx consumers treat upstream content as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Use a strict allowlist for fields passed from ComfyUI to emqx
Strip prompt-like text from any intermediate payloads
Add a manual review step before publishing messages
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model files locally, while emqx has broad network egress and HTTP API surfaces. There is no documented shared filesystem or OAuth principal, so leakage is not established. If ComfyUI outputs are forwarded into emqx messages, sensitive media or model artifacts could leave the local environment. The risk is conditional and limited by the missing bridge evidence.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are forwarded into emqx topics or HTTP payloads
IF those payloads contain sensitive images, videos, audio, or model artifacts
mitigations: Minimize payloads before forwarding to emqx
Redact or downsample media before publication
Restrict emqx topics to non-sensitive data
Log and review outbound message samples
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI does not write the filesystem or modify git state, and emqx exposes HTTP APIs with broad egress. Because the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, direct conflict is unlikely. The only plausible conflict is coordination-level contention if an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same queue or resource, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator assigns both agents to the same mutable queue or resource
IF emqx writes back into a store that ComfyUI also mutates
mitigations: Separate queues and namespaces for each agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Avoid shared mutable directories
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows and media artifacts that emqx could plausibly route or act on through HTTP APIs. The profiles do not show verification gates between them, so if emqx treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or notifications. This is an inferred interaction, but the default API-driven pathway makes the risk plausible.
conditions: IF emqx consumes ComfyUI output without validation
IF downstream automation acts on that output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a validation step before emqx acts on ComfyUI output
Require human approval for high-impact actions
Attach source metadata to every handoff
Use schema validation on all exchanged payloads
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline by default, while emqx has broad network egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to any operator-chosen data flow from local media into networked messaging. Because the pair does not itself prove a regulated-data mismatch, this remains a low, conditional concern.
conditions: IF regulated media or metadata from ComfyUI is published through emqx
IF the destination environment has stricter residency or retention rules than the source
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of emqx topics
Document retention for any forwarded media
Limit outbound destinations to approved endpoints
Review data-class mappings before deployment
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
